## Motivation

The DeepSeek-V4.1 cookbook launch uses `--enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay`. Today the server refuses to start when that flag is combined with a prefill CUDA graph, so V4.1 prefill always runs eagerly.

Eager prefill costs about 85 ms per batch on 4x B300, no matter how short the prompt is. A 590-token prompt pays it, and so does every follow-up turn of a long conversation.

Roadmap #42170 lists "Enable decoder bounded replay" with no owner. The draft #42078 fixes one piece of stale state and says it does not enable the combination. This PR covers that case as well.

## Modifications

With decoder bounded replay, the layers after the last KV source layer (the "late layers") only run over the last 128 tokens of each request. The number of those rows depends on how many requests are in the batch, not on how many tokens it has. A prefill CUDA graph has a fixed shape per token count, so the late layers could not be captured in it.

1. The late layers now have their own CUDA graphs, one per number of tail rows (128, 192, 256, 384, ... up to one window per request slot). The prefill graph runs the early layers and then replays the matching late-layer graph from a graph break. A batch is padded to the next size up, which is less than 1.5x its real tail.
2. All late-layer graphs are captured once at startup, during the first prefill graph warmup. No request triggers a capture.
3. The attention metadata for the late layers is captured once per tail size and refreshed in place on every replay.
4. When decoder bounded replay is on, the low-ratio compressor and indexer run eagerly at a graph break instead of inside the graph. The eager indexer handles any context length, so the graph is no longer limited to 16K tokens of context.
5. Capturing the graphs needs much less memory than before:
   - All graphs share one scratch buffer for padded query heads. Each graph used to keep its own (1 GB at 16K tokens).
   - Graph metadata is sized by the batch's own context instead of the model's maximum context, when nothing inside the graph needs the full width.
   - The candidate table from the indexer is dropped as soon as the late layers have used it.
6. Decode no longer sees late-layer metadata left behind by the previous prefill.
7. The checks that reject prompt logprobs and full hidden-state capture moved out of the captured code, because a replay skips that code.
8. Only the breakable backend is accepted. The `full` and `tc_piecewise` backends, ROCm, and prefill context parallelism are still rejected at startup.

Every batch now goes through the graph: any number of requests, any size up to the chunk size, any context length. Encoder bounded replay is not part of this PR.

## Accuracy Tests

4x B300, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, TP4 and EP4. Both columns run this branch. "Eager" is what the cookbook launch does today.

```bash
# eager
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --trust-remote-code --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tp 4 --ep-size 4 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 --max-running-requests 16 --enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay --disable-prefill-cuda-graph
# graph
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --trust-remote-code --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tp 4 --ep-size 4 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 --max-running-requests 16 --enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay --cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable
# DSpark rows add: --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5
python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 1319 --parallel 32
```

| GSM8K, 1319 questions | eager | graph |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no speculation | 0.906 | 0.905 |
| DSpark, block size 5 | 0.904 | 0.913 |

Each cell is one run. Repeated runs of one configuration moved between 0.900 and 0.915 while I worked on this, so these are within noise. The DSpark accept length is 3.39 in both columns.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Time to first token, median of 5 requests sent one at a time. Prompts are sent as token ids, so tokenization is not included.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Request, DSpark | eager | graph | speedup |

| 590 new tokens | 89.1 ms | 28.5 ms | 3.1x |
| 2,060 new tokens | 89.2 ms | 41.0 ms | 2.2x |
| 6,318 new tokens | 100.0 ms | 72.4 ms | 1.38x |
| 14,795 new tokens | 150.6 ms | 141.7 ms | 1.06x |

| 554 new tokens after 59.9K cached tokens | 98.2 ms | 41.4 ms | 2.4x |

| no speculation | 143.1 s | 73.7 s | 1.94x |

 **Engram.** An additive n-gram hash memory at two layers. Token ids are normalized *before* hashing, so `" The"`, `"the"` and `"THE"` cannot fork into separate rows. Its two fp8 tables are the largest single block of weight in the checkpoint, and by default they load row-sharded across the TP group, which costs an all-reduce per engram layer. `SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE=1` (**opt-in**) moves them to host memory instead: the freed HBM goes to the KV pool and output is bitwise unchanged — at the cost of host RAM, a longer load, and needing huge-page backing to keep the gather cheap. `SGLANG_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE_LAYOUT` trades the two all-reduces for page size: `shared` (the default) maps a single copy all ranks read and needs no reduce; `per_rank` splits that same table into one shard per rank and keeps the reduce, but is the only one the kernel reliably backs with 2 MiB pages.
 
-**SWA bounded replay.** Because the window store is per-layer and cheap to rebuild, it need not all be recomputed. `--enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay` (**opt-in**) runs the early layers over the whole extend and the late layers over only each request's last 128 tokens, sharing late-layer KV from source layer 20. Prefill gets materially faster. It is validated on the decode path only, refuses prompt logprobs by design, is not numerically equivalent to full prefill, and is excluded at launch with the prefill CUDA graph and with DP attention.

On Blackwell it also runs under the breakable prefill CUDA graph (**opt-in**, `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable`), which removes most of the fixed cost of a short extend. The graph serves every batch at any context length. Capturing it takes about 17 GB per GPU at the default 16384-token chunk.
 
 **Kernels.** At decode token counts these kernels are launch-bound rather than bandwidth-bound, so the work is fusion and overlap: the compressor projection, ratio-2 pooling, RoPE with fp4 quantization and indexer packing, paged fp4 indexer scoring with top-k resolved straight to cache addresses, and the mHC statistics and Sinkhorn — with compression, indexing and mHC overlapped against attention and FFN on dedicated streams. All of it is selected automatically; the environment switches it once sat behind were removed, so there is nothing to turn on. One caveat outranks the fusions: **output is not bitwise stable across batch composition today** — two default kernels are shape-guarded to a single token — and `--enable-deterministic-inference` is refused on this backend.

+    inputs: Tensors

+        """Run ``forward`` over ``inputs`` through the graph of their row count,
+        capturing it on first use. The outputs are valid until the next run."""
+        rows = inputs[0].shape[0]

+"""The DeepSeek-V4.1 late-layer tail that the late-layer CUDA graphs capture, padded to a bucket of rows."""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.deepseek_v4_backend import (
+    SWA_WINDOW,
+    LateLayerTail,
+    _prefill_graph_tail_row_buckets,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=2, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+def _padded_tail(token_indices, *, graph_rows: int) -> LateLayerTail:
+    padding = graph_rows - len(token_indices)
+    return LateLayerTail(
+        token_indices=torch.tensor(token_indices + [0] * padding),
+        positions=torch.zeros(graph_rows, dtype=torch.int64),
+        extend_seq_lens=torch.tensor([len(token_indices)], dtype=torch.int32),
+        extend_seq_lens_cpu=[len(token_indices)],
+        swa_out_cache_loc=torch.tensor(token_indices + [0] * padding),
+        padded=True,
+    )
+
+
+class TestGraphPaddedLateLayerTail(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_every_tail_fits_a_bucket_that_pads_it_by_less_than_half(self):
+        """A tail of any size must land in a captured bucket, or its batch could not
+        replay, and the bucket must stay close, or the late layers waste their win."""
+        for max_rows in (1, SWA_WINDOW, 300, 4096, 16384, 20000):
+            buckets = _prefill_graph_tail_row_buckets(max_rows)
+            self.assertEqual(buckets, sorted(set(buckets)))
+            self.assertGreaterEqual(buckets[-1], max_rows)
+        buckets = _prefill_graph_tail_row_buckets(16384)
+        for tail_rows in range(SWA_WINDOW, 16385, 37):
+            bucket = min(rows for rows in buckets if rows >= tail_rows)
+            self.assertLess(bucket, 1.5 * tail_rows)
+
+    def test_replay_refresh_keeps_the_captured_index_tensors(self):
+        """A late-layer graph reads the tail's positions and write slots by address,
+        so a replay must refill those tensors, not rebind them."""
+        captured = _padded_tail([1, 2, 3], graph_rows=4)
+        live = _padded_tail([2, 3], graph_rows=4)
+
+        refreshed = captured.refresh_for_breakable_cuda_graph_replay_(live)
+
+        self.assertIs(refreshed.token_indices, captured.token_indices)
+        self.assertIs(refreshed.positions, captured.positions)
+        self.assertIs(refreshed.swa_out_cache_loc, captured.swa_out_cache_loc)
+        self.assertEqual(refreshed.token_indices.tolist(), [2, 3, 0, 0])
+        self.assertEqual(refreshed.swa_out_cache_loc.tolist(), [2, 3, 0, 0])
+        # The DSpark target reads only the live rows of what the graph returns.
+        self.assertEqual(refreshed.live_rows(torch.arange(4)).tolist(), [0, 1])
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
